watch.definition: A small timepiece worn on the wrist or carried.
watch.exampleUsage: Hana checks her watch before work.

hour-hand.definition: The hand of an analogue clock that indicates the hour, usually shorter than the minute hand.
hour-hand.exampleUsage: The hour hand is near nine.

minute-hand.definition: The longer hand on an analog clock indicates the number of minutes past the hour.
minute-hand.exampleUsage: The minute hand is on the twelve mark.

second-hand.definition: The thin hand on an analog clock or watch that shows seconds.
second-hand.exampleUsage: The second hand moves around the dial.

clock-face.definition: The dial or front surface of a clock where time is shown.
clock-face.exampleUsage: The clock face has clear tick marks.

digital-clock.definition: An electronic clock that displays the hour and minute as numbers instead of using hands on a dial.

sundial.definition: A device that uses the sun’s shadow to show time.
sundial.exampleUsage: The sundial stands in the garden.

hourglass.definition: A device that measures a set period as sand flows between two glass chambers.
hourglass.exampleUsage: The sand flows through the hourglass.

second.definition: A unit of time equal to one sixtieth of a minute.

minute.definition: A unit of time equal to 60 seconds or 1/60th of an hour.

half-hour.exampleUsage: The class lasts half an hour.

quarter-hour.exampleUsage: The break lasts a quarter hour.

noon.definition: Twelve o'clock in the middle of the day.

midnight.definition: Twelve o'clock at night, between two days.
midnight.exampleUsage: The next day begins at midnight.

dawn.definition: The time in the morning when daylight first appears.

dusk.definition: The evening time when daylight is fading towards darkness.
dusk.exampleUsage: The sky grows darker at dusk.

twilight.definition: The light and time when the sun is below the horizon before sunrise or after sunset.

o-clock.definition: Used after a number to state an exact hour on the clock.
o-clock.exampleUsage: The meeting starts at nine o’clock.

half-past.definition: Thirty minutes after a stated hour.
half-past.exampleUsage: The break starts at half past nine.

quarter-past.definition: Fifteen minutes after a stated hour.
quarter-past.exampleUsage: Hana arrives at quarter past nine.

quarter-to.definition: Fifteen minutes before the next stated hour.
quarter-to.exampleUsage: The train leaves at quarter to ten.

five-past.definition: Five minutes after a stated hour.
five-past.exampleUsage: The bus arrives at five past two.

ten-past.definition: Ten minutes after a stated hour.
ten-past.exampleUsage: We leave at ten past seven.

twenty-past.definition: Twenty minutes after a stated hour.
twenty-past.exampleUsage: The meeting ends at twenty past four.

five-to.definition: Five minutes before the next stated hour.
five-to.exampleUsage: Hana arrives at five to nine.

ten-to.definition: Ten minutes before the next stated hour.
ten-to.exampleUsage: The bus leaves at ten to six.

sharp.definition: Exactly at a stated time, without being early or late.
sharp.exampleUsage: The class starts at nine sharp.

morning.definition: The time period between dawn and noon.

afternoon.definition: The part of the day between noon and evening.
afternoon.exampleUsage: The next meeting is in the afternoon.

evening.definition: The latter part of the day (the period of decreasing daylight from late afternoon until nightfall).

night.definition: The dark part of the day between evening and morning.

sunrise.definition: The time when the sun first appears in the sky.

sunset.definition: The time when the sun disappears below the horizon.
sunset.exampleUsage: They watch the sunset from the window.

midday.definition: The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock.

late-night.definition: The period near the end of the evening or during the first hours after midnight.
late-night.exampleUsage: The last programme is shown late at night.

early-morning.definition: The first part of the morning, around sunrise.
early-morning.exampleUsage: Karim walks to work in the early morning.

nightfall.definition: The time in the evening when darkness begins.

a-m-.definition: Used with times from midnight up to, but not including, noon.
a-m-.exampleUsage: The meeting starts at nine a.m.

p-m-.definition: Used with times from noon up to, but not including, midnight.

on-time.definition: Arriving on time means reaching a place at the agreed or expected moment.

early.definition: At or near the beginning of a period of time or course of events or before the usual or expected time.

late.definition: After the expected or planned time.

ahead-of-time.definition: It refers to doing something earlier than the customary or anticipated time.
ahead-of-time.exampleUsage: The team finishes the task ahead of time.

behind-schedule.definition: Later than the planned time or not progressing as quickly as planned.

overtime.definition: Time worked beyond the usual working hours.

countdown.definition: A count towards zero showing the time remaining before an event.
countdown.exampleUsage: The countdown shows ten seconds remaining.

stopwatch.definition: A watch that measures how long an activity takes.
stopwatch.exampleUsage: The stopwatch measures the test duration.

clock.definition: A device for showing the time.
clock.exampleUsage: The clock is on the wall.

alarm-clock.definition: A clock that gives a signal at a chosen time.
alarm-clock.exampleUsage: The alarm clock rings at seven.
